sourceRefs.locator: AT-OeStA/HHStA UR AUR 9228. Dates and places, regest, extent and seal description: only the Nuremberg part of this copy bears a golden seal of 66.6–67.2 mm in diameter.
Panel Die Goldene Bulle. Chapters 1–23 at Nuremberg and 24–31 at Metz in 1356, name from the gold seal, surviving original copies.
pp. 365–366, especially n. 46 quoting ch. 31. Languages for lay electoral heirs, age requirements, Latin and the interpretation of the Slavic language as Czech.
Ch. 31, two final paragraphs. Early language instruction for the four lay electoral families and the choice between sending children away and engaging experienced teachers at home.
GeonameId 2994160, town centre coordinates 49.11911 N, 6.17269 E.

note.de: Die Schlusskapitel der Goldenen Bulle entstehen in Metz. Kapitel 31 regelt die sprachliche Erziehung der Erben der vier weltlichen Kurfürsten.
note.en: The final chapters of the Golden Bull are issued at Metz. Chapter 31 deals with language education for the heirs of the four lay electors.
